The '''7th House of Representatives''' is the current meeting of the lower chamber of the [[Federal Parliament of Nepal]], the [[House of Representatives (Nepal)|House of Representatives]]. Members took their oath of office on 26 March 2026,<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Newly elected HoR members to take oath today |url=https://risingnepaldaily.com/news/77742 |access-date=2026-04-01 |website=GorakhaPatra}}</ref> following the [[2026 Nepalese general election|general election held on 5 March 2026]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-03-13 |title=Nepal election results - Balendra Shah's party wins in a landslide |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cev7z9802zjo |access-date=2026-03-16 |website=www.bbc.com |language=en-GB}}</ref>

== Parliamentary term ==
The final results of the election were presented to the [[President of Nepal|president]] on 20 March 2026 by the [[Election Commission (Nepal)|Election Commission]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=EC submits poll report to President |url=https://risingnepaldaily.com/news/77413 |access-date=2026-04-01 |website=GorakhaPatra}}</ref>  

The oldest member of the House of Representatives, [[Arjun Narasingha KC|Arjun Narasingha K. C.]], was administered the oath of office and secrecy on 25 March, following which K. C. administered the oath to the remaining members.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2026-03-25 |title=Arjun Narsingh KC sworn in as senior-most HoR member |url=https://thehimalayantimes.com/kathmandu/arjun-narsingh-kc-sworn-in-as-senior-most-hor-member |access-date=2026-04-01 |website=The Himalayan Times |language=en}}</ref>  

A joint session of the Federal Parliament was called for 2 April 2026 by the president on the recommendation of the [[Balen Shah cabinet|cabinet]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Government recommends summoning federal parliament session on Thursday |url=https://kathmandupost.com/national/2026/03/30/government-recommends-summoning-house-session-on-thursday |access-date=2026-04-01 |website=kathmandupost.com |language=English}}</ref>  

On 5 April 2026, [[Dol Prasad Aryal]] from [[Rastriya Swatantra Party]] was elected unopposed as the [[Speaker of the House of Representatives (Nepal)|Speaker]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=5 April 2026 |title=Dol Prasad Aryal elected House Speaker unopposed |url=https://thehimalayantimes.com/kathmandu/dol-prasad-aryal-elected-house-speaker-unopposed |access-date=10 April 2026 |website=[[The Himalayan Times]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=6 April 2026 |title=DP Aryal elected House Speaker |url=https://risingnepaldaily.com/news/78302 |access-date=10 April 2026 |website=[[The Rising Nepal]] |language=en}}</ref> [[Ruby Kumari Thakur]] from [[Shram Sanskriti Party]] was elected as the [[Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives (Nepal)|deputy speaker]].<ref>{{cite news |title=25-Year-Old Ruby Kumari Thakur Elected Deputy Speaker |url=https://en.setopati.com/political/166240 |work=Setopati |date=9 April 2026 |access-date=10 April 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Rubi Kumari Thakur Becomes Nepal's Youngest Deputy Speaker, Wins HoR Post with RSP Backing |url=https://www.latestly.com/world/rubi-kumari-thakur-becomes-nepals-youngest-deputy-speaker-wins-hor-post-with-rsp-backing-7388475.html |work=Latestly |access-date=10 April 2026}}</ref>

== Officeholders ==
=== Presiding officers ===
* '''[[Speaker of the House of Representatives (Nepal)|Speaker]]''': Rt. Hon. [[Dol Prasad Aryal]], [[Rastriya Swatantra Party]] 
** '''[[Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives (Nepal)|Deputy Speaker]]''': Hon. [[Ruby Kumari Thakur]], [[Shram Sanskriti Party]]

== Sessions ==
The [[House of Representatives (Nepal)|House of Representatives]] has three sessions in a year; budget session, monsoon session and winter session. The following sessions were held of the 7th House of Representatives.
{{sticky header}}
{| class="wikitable sortable sticky-header" width:90%;"
|-
! Session
! Date
! Key Events
! Ref.
|-
| style="text-align: center;" |Oath
|25−26 March 2026
|{{bulletlist| Senior-most member [[Arjun Narsingh KC]] (78 years) first took the oath from President [[Ram Chandra Paudel]] on March 25, and then administered the oath to other lawmakers on March 26.}}
|<ref>{{cite web |url=https://ekantipur.com/news/2026/03/26/en/senior-member-of-the-house-of-representatives-kc-administers-oath-to-lawmakers-24-57.html |title=Senior member of the House of Representatives KC administers oath to newly elected MPs |date=26 March 2026 |access-date=6 April 2026 |work=[[Kantipur (daily)|Ekantipur]]}}</ref>
|-
| rowspan="3" style="text-align: center;" | 1<sup>st</sup>
| 2 April 2026
| {{bulletlist| [[Inaugural]] [[Session (parliamentary procedure)|Session]] of the 7th House of Representatives.}}
| <ref>{{Cite web |date=2 April 2026 |title=सूचनापत्र २०८२-१२-१९ |url=https://hr.parliament.gov.np/np/notices/1775362980 |access-date=15 May 2026 |website=[[House of Representatives (Nepal)|House of Representatives]] Parliamentary Notices |language=ne}}</ref>
|-
| 5 April 2026
| {{bulletlist| [[Dol Prasad Aryal]] elected as [[Speaker of the House of Representatives (Nepal)|Speaker of the House of Representatives]].}}
| <ref>{{Cite web |date=5 April 2026 |title=सूचनापत्र २०८२-१२-२२ |url=https://hr.parliament.gov.np/np/notices/1775451727 |access-date=15 May 2026 |website=[[House of Representatives (Nepal)|House of Representatives]] Parliamentary Notices |language=ne}}</ref>
|-
|10 April 2026
|
{{bulletlist|[[Ram Chandra Paudel|President Ram Chandra Paudel]] addressed the joint session of the Federal Parliament.|[[Ruby Kumari Thakur]] elected as [[Speaker of the House of Representatives (Nepal)|Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives]].|[[Dol Prasad Aryal|Speaker DP Aryal]] formed the [[Federal Parliament of Nepal|Parliamentary committees]].|President Ram Chandra Paudel prorogued the Inaugural Session.}}
|<ref>{{Cite web |date=10 April 2026 |title=सूचनापत्र २०८२-१२-२७ |url=https://hr.parliament.gov.np/np/notices/1776406438 |access-date=15 May 2026 |website=[[House of Representatives (Nepal)|House of Representatives]] Parliamentary Notices |language=ne}}</ref>
|-
| rowspan="11" style="text-align: center;" | 2<sup>nd</sup>
|11 May 2026
|
{{bulletlist||The government tabled 8 ordinances, starting the constitutional 60-day window for parliamentary ratification: ''Public Procurement (Second Amendment) Ordinance, 2083'', ''Special Provisions on the Removal of Public Officials Ordinance, 2083'', ''Constitutional Council (Function, Duties, Powers and Procedures) (First Amendment) Ordinance, 2083'', ''Prevention of Money Laundering (Third Amendment) Ordinance, 2083'', ''Amendment of Certain Nepal Acts Ordinance, 2083'', ''Cooperatives (First Amendment) Ordinance, 2083'', ''Amendment of Certain Nepal Acts Relating to Health Sciences Institutes Ordinance, 2083'', and ''Amendment of Certain Nepal Acts Relating to Universities Ordinance, 2083''.|[[Ram Chandra Paudel|President Ram Chandra Paudel]] addressed a joint session of the parliament to deliver the government's policy and programme for the fiscal year 2083/84.}}
|<ref>{{Cite web |date=11 May 2026 |title=सूचनापत्र २०८३-१-२८ |url=https://hr.parliament.gov.np/np/notices/1778502060 |access-date=15 May 2026 |website=[[House of Representatives (Nepal)|House of Representatives]] Parliamentary Notices |language=ne}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=संसद्‌मा पेश भए ८ अध्यादेश |url=https://ekantipur.com/politics/2026/05/11/8-ordinances-introduced-in-parliament-17-30.html |access-date=2026-05-12 |website=Ekantipur |language=ne}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Nepal outlines 7 percent growth ambition under broad reform agenda, challenges remain |url=https://kathmandupost.com/money/2026/05/12/nepal-outlines-7-percent-growth-ambition-under-broad-reform-agenda-challenges-remain |access-date=2026-05-12 |website=kathmandupost.com |language=English}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Govt unveils policies and programmes of 2026/27 |url=https://risingnepaldaily.com/news/80101 |access-date=2026-05-12 |website=GorakhaPatra}}</ref>
|-
|12 May 2026
|{{Bulleted list|[[Minister of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs (Nepal)|Minister for Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs]] [[Sobita Gautam]] tabled the ''Agreement on Mutual Legal Assistance in Criminal Matters'' concluded between the [[Government of Nepal]] and the [[Government of India]] to the house.}}
|<ref>{{Cite web |date=12 May 2026 |title=सूचनापत्र २०८३-१-२९ |url=https://hr.parliament.gov.np/np/notices/1778583722 |access-date=15 May 2026 |website=[[House of Representatives (Nepal)|House of Representatives]] Parliamentary Notices |language=ne}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=नेपाल-भारत पारस्परिक कानूनी सहायता सम्झौता प्रतिनिधि सभामा पेश |url=https://gorkhapatraonline.com/news/205533 |access-date=2026-05-12 |website=GorakhaPatra}}</ref>
|-
|14 May 2026
|{{Bulleted list|2=[[Minister of Finance (Nepal)|Minister of Finance]] [[Swarnim Wagle]] answered questions raised during the general discussion on the government's policy and programme for the fiscal year 2083/84, on behalf of [[Balen Shah|Prime Minister Balen Shah]], despite obstruction from opposition parties demanding attendance of the prime minister.|3=The government's policy and programme for the fiscal year 2083/84 passed by unanimity despite obstruction from opposition parties.}}
|<ref>{{Cite web |date=14 May 2026 |title=सूचनापत्र २०८३-१-३१ |url=https://hr.parliament.gov.np/np/notices/1778833204 |access-date=15 May 2026 |website=[[House of Representatives (Nepal)|House of Representatives]] Parliamentary Notices |language=ne}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Opposition demands Speaker compel PM to attend parliament |url=https://kathmandupost.com/politics/2026/05/15/opposition-demands-speaker-compel-pm-to-attend-parliament |access-date=2026-05-15 |website=kathmandupost.com |language=English}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-08-08 |title=HoR endorses govt policies and programmes amid opposition protests, criticism |url=https://myrepublica.nagariknetwork.com/news/hor-endorses-govt-policies-and-programmes-amid-opposition-protests-criticis-86-17.html |access-date=2026-05-15 |website=myrepublica.nagariknetwork.com |language=English}}</ref>
|-
|21 May 2026
|
* The ''Alternative Development Finance Mobilization Bill, 2082'' passed by a majority vote, amidst the disruption by opposition parties demanding the parliamentary accountability from the prime minister.
|<ref>{{Cite web |date= |title=सूचनापत्र २०८३-०२-०७ |url=https://hr.parliament.gov.np/np/notices/1779341853 |website=House of Representatives, Nepal|access-date=22 May 2026}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=HoR passes 'Alternative Development Finance Mobilization Bill, 2082' |url=https://risingnepaldaily.com/news/80651 |access-date=2026-05-22 |website=GorakhaPatra}}</ref>
|-
|27 May 2026
|
* Minister of Finance Swarnim Wagle presented the Economic Survey of the fiscal year 2082/83 to the House. The report projected a national economic growth rate of 3.85%, estimated the total size of Nepal's economy at NRs. 6.6 trillion, and noted that per capita gross national income had reached US$ 1,535. It also revealed that public debt stood at NRs. 2.878 trillion, representing 43.6% of the GDP.
|<ref>{{Cite web |date= |title=सूचनापत्र २०८३-०२-१३ |url=https://hr.parliament.gov.np/np/notices/1780046825 |website=House of Representatives, Nepal |access-date=29 May 2026}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Economic Survey made public: growth estimated to be 3.85% |url=https://risingnepaldaily.com/news/80968 |access-date=2026-05-27 |website=GorakhaPatra}}</ref>
|-
|29 May 2026
|
* [[Minister of Finance (Nepal)|Minister of Finance]] [[Swarnim Wagle]] addressed a joint session of the Federal Parliament to deliver the annual budget speech, detailing the estimates of revenue and expenditure for the fiscal year 2083/84. Following the address, the Minister formally tabled the budget document and introduced the ''Finance Bill, 2083'' to initiate the legislative process for the government's tax and revenue proposals.
|<ref>{{Cite web |title=संयुक्त बैठको सूचना पत्र २०८३-०२-१५ |url=https://hr.parliament.gov.np/np/notices/1780129046 |access-date=1 Jun 2026 |website=House of Representatives, Nepal}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=सूचनापत्र २०८३-०२-१५ |url=https://hr.parliament.gov.np/np/notices/1780128878 |access-date=1 Jun 2026 |website=House of Representatives, Nepal}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Govt unveils Rs. 2124 bn budget for FY 2026/27 |url=https://risingnepaldaily.com/news/81104 |access-date=2026-05-30 |website=GorakhaPatra}}</ref>
|-
|31 May 2026
|
* [[Prime Minister of Nepal|Prime Minister]] [[Balen Shah|Balendra Shah]] participated in an impromptu question-and-answer session following prolonged opposition demands. The proceeding drew immediate procedural objections from opposition benches alleging a breach of the ''House of Representatives Rules, 2079''. The session escalated into a significant political debate after the Prime Minister expressed surprise that recent findings indicated mutual encroachment of land along certain border areas by both India and Nepal, rather than it being one-sided. Opposition lawmakers strongly rejected the characterization, demanding the Prime Minister either substantiate the claim with evidence or issue a formal retraction and apology.
* Later in the same sitting, the House passed the ''House of Representatives Rules, 2083'' by a majority vote amidst intense opposition protests. The session descended into physical confrontation as several opposition lawmakers attempted to charge the Speaker and storm the central rostrum, forcing security marshals to form a physical barrier to protect the dais and restore order.
|<ref>{{Cite web |title=सूचनापत्र २०८३-०२-१७ |url=https://hr.parliament.gov.np/np/notices/1780554628 |access-date=28 June 2026 |website=House of Representatives, Nepal}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Border dispute will be solved through diplomatic efforts: PM Shah |url=https://risingnepaldaily.com/news/81208 |access-date=2026-06-02 |website=GorakhaPatra}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=PM Shah says that just like India has encroached on Nepali land, Nepal has also encroached on India’s |url=https://kathmandupost.com/national/2026/05/31/pm-shah-says-all-commission-reports-including-gen-z-protest-report-will-be-implemented |access-date=2026-06-02 |website=kathmandupost.com |language=English}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Opposition parties demand PM Shah apologise over border remarks, threaten continued House obstruction |url=https://kathmandupost.com/national/2026/06/01/opposition-parties-demand-pm-shah-apologise-over-border-remarks-threaten-continued-house-obstruction |access-date=2026-06-02 |website=kathmandupost.com |language=English}}</ref>
|-
|10 June 2026
|
* Following a ten-day deadlock, parliament finally resumed after [[Minister of Foreign Affairs (Nepal)|Minister of Foreign Affairs]] [[Shisir Khanal]] clarified the Prime Minister's controversial statement regarding the border dispute. Although the PM refused to yield to opposition demands, the clarification paved way for the house to reopen and transition into general discussion on the FY 2083/84 annual budget.
|<ref>{{Cite web |title=सूचनापत्र २०८३-०२-२७ |url=https://hr.parliament.gov.np/np/notices/1781157301 |access-date=19 June 2026 |website=House of Representatives, Nepal}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Obstruction of opposition parties ends, HoR meeting underway |url=https://risingnepaldaily.com/news/81698 |access-date=2026-06-19 |website=GorakhaPatra}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=PM's statement on border related to cross border occupation: Foreign Minister Khanal |url=https://risingnepaldaily.com/news/81702 |access-date=2026-06-19 |website=GorakhaPatra}}</ref>
|-
|18 June 2026
|
* The House passed the ''Appropriation Bill, 2083''. The proposal, tabled by [[Minister of Finance (Nepal)|Minister of Finance]] [[Swarnim Wagle]], was formally endorsed following the conclusion of the ministry-wise budget reviews and subsequent ministerial responses to lawmakers' inquiries.
|<ref>{{Cite web |title=सूचनापत्र २०८३-०३-०४ |url=https://hr.parliament.gov.np/np/notices/1781850614 |access-date=28 June 2026 |website=House of Representatives, Nepal}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Lower House passes Appropriation Bill |url=https://risingnepaldaily.com/news/82122 |access-date=2026-06-19 |website=GorakhaPatra}}</ref>
|-
|28 June 2026
|
* Successfully concluding the budget process for the upcoming fiscal year 2083/84, the House passed both the ''Finance Bill, 2083'' and ''National Debt Recovery Bill, 2083''. 
|<ref>{{Cite web |title=सूचनापत्र २०८३-०३-१४ |url=https://hr.parliament.gov.np/np/notices/1782623052 |access-date=2 July 2026 |website=House of Representatives, Nepal}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=HoR passes Finance Bill, 2083 |url=https://risingnepaldaily.com/news/82625 |access-date=2026-06-28 |website=GorakhaPatra}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=HoR passes Bill to Raise Public Debt |url=https://risingnepaldaily.com/news/82628 |access-date=2026-06-28 |website=GorakhaPatra}}</ref>
|-
|2 July 2026
|
* Continuing its legislative proceedings, the House passed four ordinance replacement bills: ''Public Procurement (Second Amendment) Bill, 2083'', ''Prevention of Money Laundering (Third Amendment) Bill, 2083'', ''Cooperatives (First Amendment) Bill, 2083'' and ''Bill to Amend Certain Nepal Acts Relating to the Institute of Health Sciences, 2083''.
|<ref>{{Cite web |title=HoR passes Public Procurement (Second Amendment) Bill |url=https://risingnepaldaily.com/news/82838 |access-date=2026-07-02 |website=GorakhaPatra}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Prevention of Money Laundering (Third Amendment) Bill, 2083 passed |url=https://risingnepaldaily.com/news/82842 |access-date=2026-07-02 |website=GorakhaPatra}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=HoR: Cooperative (First Amendment) Bill, 2083 passed |url=https://risingnepaldaily.com/news/82850 |access-date=2026-07-02 |website=GorakhaPatra}}</ref>
|}
